title: pulse
subtitle: Financial news sentiment dashboard
overview: A dashboard that reads financial news the way a trader skims a terminal — fast, and with a sense of which way the mood is turning.
body: Markets react to news faster than any person can read it, and most sentiment tools quietly fail on financial text — a general-purpose model like VADER treats words like "beat," "short," "bearish," or "guidance cut" as neutral or plain negative, when in a market context they carry precise, often opposite, signals. Pulse exists to read financial news the way someone who actually trades would.

The pipeline is straightforward on paper: news comes in, gets scored for sentiment, and surfaces on a live dashboard organised around tickers and topics. The scoring stage is where the real work is — v1 used VADER, and v2 replaces it entirely with FinBERT, a transformer pre-trained on financial language, so sentiment reads as domain-aware rather than dictionary-driven.

Swapping the whole sentiment engine rather than patching the old lexicon was a deliberate call — it's the difference between rule-based guessing and something that's actually learned what financial language means. v2 also rebuilds the frontend from scratch in Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind, because a dashboard that's right but slow to read isn't actually useful.
Actively building v2 — this is one of the core anchors of what I'm working on right now.
